question: What is a major long-term risk for someone staying on an extremely strict low-fat diet for months?

options.A: Sudden increase in digestive enzyme output
options.B: Permanent enlargement of the stomach
options.C: Deficiencies in fat-soluble vitamins
options.D: Excessive accumulation of muscle mass

explanation: Without a little healthy dietary fat over time, the body struggles to absorb key vitamins like A, D, E, and K. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T005#GNS227_U6_T005_h8)

question: Why can a strong family preference for male children negatively impact a mother's health?

options.A: It forces women into continuous pregnancies until a son is born, straining their bodies
options.B: It reduces the financial income of the father drastically
options.C: It causes hospitals to refuse treatment to female newborns
options.D: It encourages the use of modern contraceptives

explanation: Constant, closely spaced pregnancies driven by the pressure to have a son really wear down a mother's body and deplete her nutrients. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h4)

question: What is the recommended angle for lifting the head of the bed for a patient on a mechanical ventilator?

options.A: 30 to 45 degrees
options.B: 0 to 15 degrees
options.C: 60 to 75 degrees
options.D: 90 degrees sitting upright

explanation: Keeping the bed raised between 30 and 45 degrees uses gravity to help stop spit or stomach juices from sliding down into the lungs. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T10#GNS321_U2_T10_h4)

question: Why do modern ORS packets use trisodium citrate instead of bicarbonate?

options.A: It gives the solution a sweeter taste for children
options.B: It speeds up the digestion of complex fats
options.C: It directly kills the parasites living in the gut
options.D: It makes the dry powder more stable during storage

explanation: Citrate handles hot, humid weather much better than bicarbonate, which means the ORS packets last longer without breaking down in our climate. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T18#GNS215_U6_T18_h3)

question: Who is considered the primary client for a community health nurse?

options.A: The attending physician
options.B: The hospitalized patient
options.C: The local government authority
options.D: The entire community

explanation: Great job thinking big picture! Unlike bedside nursing that focuses on one patient at a time, community health nurses look at the health of the whole population in an area. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T7#GNS225_U2_T7_h1)

question: What is the main goal of injection safety in nursing?

options.A: To prevent harm to the patient, nurse, and community
options.B: To ensure medications dissolve faster in the bloodstream
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of hospital supplies
options.D: To speed up the delivery of emergency medications

explanation: You got this! Injection safety is all about protecting everyone from accidental injury or infection. Keeping patients, ourselves, and our communities safe always comes first. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T3#GNS122_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which type of scale is best suited for an adult patient who is completely unable to stand?

options.A: A specialized chair or bed scale
options.B: A standard beam balance scale
options.C: A hanging infant spring scale
options.D: A flat digital floor scale

explanation: Chair and bed scales allow nurses to obtain accurate weights for immobile patients without forcing them to stand. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h2)

question: Why is giving quick feedback so important when teaching clinical skills?

options.A: It ensures the school receives government funding
options.B: It prevents students from asking clinical questions
options.C: It replaces the need for formal written examinations
options.D: It connects the performance directly to the learning moment

explanation: If someone tells you what you did right or wrong right away, your brain connects with it immediately before you forget the details. [learn more](GST321_U8_T2#GST321_U8_T2_h4)

question: Which health problem is a woman more likely to face later in life if she had preeclampsia during pregnancy?

options.A: Higher lifetime risk of heart disease
options.B: Chronic chest allergies
options.C: Permanent blindness in both eyes
options.D: Getting chronic kidney stones

explanation: Having preeclampsia is like a stress test for the body's blood vessels, meaning these women have a higher chance of heart and blood pressure issues later in life. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T019#GNS226_U2_T019_h7)

question: Why must a client eat a diet rich in carbohydrates for three days before a GTT?

options.A: To make sure the stomach is completely full before drinking the sweet syrup
options.B: To prevent false-positive results caused by low carbohydrate intake
options.C: To test how fast the liver can store extra glycogen reserves
options.D: To ensure the patient has plenty of energy to sit still during the test

explanation: If a patient restricts carbs beforehand, their body stops producing enough insulin, causing a fake diabetic spike during the test. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h3)

question: How do sperm travel forward through the vas deferens during ejaculation?

options.A: By using their own flagella tails
options.B: By floating downward with gravity
options.C: Through constant blood pressure surges
options.D: Through muscular wave contractions

explanation: The walls of the vas deferens have smooth muscles that squeeze in gentle wave motions (peristalsis) to push the sperm right along. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T2#GNS121_U4_T2_h4)

question: Which of these is a good example of modifying the environment to control disease carriers?

options.A: Administering routine oral polio vaccines to newborn infants
options.B: Draining stagnant water pools where mosquitoes lay their eggs
options.C: Treating confirmed malaria patients with appropriate antimalarial drugs
options.D: Distributing insecticide-treated bed nets to pregnant mothers

explanation: Well done! Changing the physical surroundings—like clearing out standing water—stops mosquitoes from breeding there in the first place. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h3)

question: Why is keeping the 'cold chain' so important when handling polio vaccines?

options.A: To activate the chemical preservatives inside the glass vial
options.B: To keep the liquid vaccine from freezing solid in storage
options.C: To prevent the heat-sensitive vaccine from losing its potency
options.D: To ensure the vaccine changes color before administration

explanation: Spot on! Polio vaccines are fragile biological products that break down and become useless if exposed to too much heat. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h5)

question: You walk into a ward and see that your patient's traction weights are resting on the floor. What is your very next move?

options.A: Lift the weights and ensure they hang freely
options.B: Remove the traction apparatus immediately
options.C: Add more weight to make up for lost time
options.D: Document that the therapy is finished

explanation: Quick thinking! Just lift them up so they hang free again, and traction is instantly restored. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T12#GNS221_U1_T12_h4)

question: How does surveillance help us check if a vaccination campaign worked?

options.A: By calculating the exact salary of the nurses giving the shots
options.B: By showing whether disease rates drop after the vaccines are given
options.C: By tracking how many nurses attended the training workshop
options.D: By testing the chemical composition of vaccine vials

explanation: By keeping track of sickness rates over time, public health teams can easily tell if giving out those vaccines actually stopped the disease. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h2)

question: A mother stops bringing her baby for immunizations because health workers shouted at her for arriving late last month. What type of factor caused this default?

options.A: Severe natural vaccine reactions
options.B: System-related facility barriers
options.C: Genetic predisposition to disease
options.D: Biological immunity resistance

explanation: Poor staff attitudes and hostile clinic environments are system-level barriers that drive caregivers away from health facilities. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h2)

question: What statistical value is commonly used to measure the internal consistency of a questionnaire?

options.A: Cronbach's alpha
options.B: Celsius scale
options.C: Body mass index
options.D: P-value index

explanation: Cronbach's alpha is the standard statistical test used to check if items within a scale relate well to one another. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h7)

question: A patient with severe malaria arrives late at a clinic because they couldn't afford transport or consultation fees. What economic factor is mainly to blame?

options.A: Excessive government spending on preventative health education
options.B: Too many nurses working in rural primary health centers
options.C: High reliance on out-of-pocket health expenditure
options.D: An oversupply of subsidized pharmaceutical drugs in local markets

explanation: When patients have to pay cash out of pocket right away, it creates a financial barrier that delays life-saving care. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h6)

question: How is rehabilitation different from acute care?

options.A: Acute care focuses on vaccination, while rehabilitation treats chronic illness
options.B: Acute care saves lives and cures disease, while rehabilitation restores independence
options.C: Acute care stops all medication, while rehabilitation starts new drugs
options.D: Acute care provides lifelong shelter, while rehabilitation offers short stays

explanation: Spot on! Acute care is all about handling immediate emergencies and stopping disease, whereas rehabilitation steps in to help patients regain their lost abilities so they can live freely again. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h1)

question: How is a personal health record (PHR) different from a hospital patient portal?

options.A: A portal is stored on a patient's personal smartphone without any hospital connection
options.B: A personal health record can only be viewed by doctors inside intensive care units
options.C: A personal health record is legally owned and controlled by the nursing staff
options.D: A personal health record is managed entirely by the patient, while a portal links directly to a hospital's EHR

explanation: Fantastic! Think of a PHR as something the patient completely controls themselves, while a portal is a window into the hospital's official system. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the function of an audit trail in an electronic health record system?

options.A: To measure how fast patients recover from surgical procedures
options.B: To calculate the exact financial cost of hospital supplies used daily
options.C: To track and record every user who opens, views, or edits a patient file
options.D: To automatically generate monthly nursing staff duty rosters and shifts

explanation: Audit trails record digital footprints, showing precisely who accessed a patient's record and when, which deters unauthorized snooping. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why is proper technique so important when doing venepuncture?

options.A: To eliminate the need for hand washing
options.B: To reduce the cost of laboratory reagents
options.C: To prevent patient harm and protect sample quality
options.D: To speed up the patient discharge time

explanation: Taking your time to use the right technique keeps your patient safe from injury and ensures the lab gets an accurate, unblemished sample. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h1)

question: Which tool is most frequently used to gather opinions from large groups in descriptive research?

options.A: Laboratory blood cultures
options.B: Surgical biopsy procedures
options.C: Surveys and questionnaires
options.D: Randomized drug trials

explanation: When you need to hear from many people quickly, questionnaires and surveys are the easiest and most practical tools to use. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h4)

question: Why is protecting health information harder in a home setting than in a hospital?

options.A: Patients demand that their records be posted on the front door
options.B: Family members, visitors, and housemates are frequently present in the care area
options.C: Home health nurses are not bound by legal privacy rules
options.D: Hospitals do not have strict privacy laws

explanation: Spot on! Homes are busy places with people walking in and out, making it easy for others to accidentally overhear health matters or see your notes. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T10#GNS324_U1_T10_h6)

question: Why must nurses regularly check the expiration dates of medicines in a clinic pharmacy?

options.A: To decide which nurse gets a promotion
options.B: To prevent patients from receiving expired or ineffective drugs
options.C: To make the medicine shelves look neat and colorful
options.D: To increase the financial profit of the local government

explanation: Expired medications may lose their chemical potency or become toxic, harming the patient instead of curing them. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h9)

question: Why do middle adolescents often take big risks even when they know the rules?

options.A: They lack the physical capacity to understand danger
options.B: Peer pressure is the only cause of adolescent accidents
options.C: The emotional brain matures faster than the impulse-control brain center
options.D: Their long-term memory is completely deactivated

explanation: You got it! The emotional part of the brain develops faster than the part that controls impulses, making them crave exciting rewards while struggling to put on the brakes. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T3#GNS312_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is the most crucial instruction for a patient who has just used an epinephrine auto-injector?

options.A: Take a hot shower to wash off any remaining allergen
options.B: Seek immediate emergency medical help at a hospital
options.C: Eat a small meal to restore normal blood sugar levels
options.D: Go to sleep quietly to let the medication take full effect

explanation: Epinephrine buys precious time, but it wears off. Every patient who uses an auto-injector must head straight to the hospital for monitoring. [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h7)

question: What is a key requirement for the Lactational Amenorrhea Method to remain effective as contraception?

options.A: Taking daily iron supplements along with herbal teas
options.B: Switching to infant formula feeds after the first month
options.C: Exclusive breastfeeding without supplementary feeds and no return of menses
options.D: Using male condoms during every third act of sexual intercourse

explanation: LAM relies on frequent suckling hormones to suppress ovulation, but it only works if breastfeeding is exclusive and menstruation has not resumed. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h7)

question: What must a cell do if it makes steroid hormones and suddenly receives a continuous call to release more?

options.A: It must rapidly synthesize new hormone molecules from cholesterol on the spot
options.B: It pumps stored hormones out of the cytoplasm using ATP energy channels
options.C: It opens storage vesicle gates to release a large backup supply of ready hormones
options.D: It stops producing hormones until old supplies are cleared from the blood

explanation: Unlike peptide hormones, steroid hormones aren't stored in large stockpiles. If the body needs more right now, the cell has to manufacture them fresh from cholesterol immediately. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T3#GNS211_U1_T3_h5)

question: Which vaccines are typically given to a newborn baby immediately at birth?

options.A: Pentavalent and Rotavirus
options.B: Tetanus toxoid and Hepatitis A
options.C: Measles and Yellow Fever
options.D: BCG and Oral Polio Vaccine

explanation: Newborns receive BCG for tuberculosis protection and OPV zero right at birth before leaving the health facility. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h2)

question: Which part of the joint capsule is responsible for making synovial fluid?

options.A: Synovial membrane
options.B: Periosteum
options.C: Fibrous layer
options.D: Articular cartilage

explanation: Correct! The inner lining of the joint capsule is the synovial membrane, and it constantly produces that slippery lubricating fluid. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h4)

question: What two signs tell us a mother is truly in preterm labour?

options.A: Regular contractions and progressive cervical change
options.B: Complete rupture of membranes and heavy bleeding
options.C: Severe headache and blurred vision in the third trimester
options.D: High blood pressure and sudden swelling of the feet

explanation: Spotting true labour means looking for both regular tummy tightening (contractions) and signs that the cervix is actually opening up. Great job learning the clinical markers! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h1)

question: What is a common problem when excess nitrogen and phosphorus from sewage enter water bodies?

options.A: Complete purification of the water within twenty-four hours
options.B: Harmful algal blooms that can release toxins into the water
options.C: An increase in clear visibility and deep-water plant growth
options.D: Immediate freezing of the water surface during warm seasons

explanation: Nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus act like plant fertilizer in water bodies, triggering massive algal overgrowths that block sunlight and can release dangerous toxins. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h7)

question: A patient feels heavy, has aching muscles, and can't sleep well—yet tests show no physical disease. What matches this?

options.A: Bacterial meningitis
options.B: Acute appendicitis
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Neurasthenia

explanation: Brilliant! When physical weakness and poor sleep won't go away and tests are clear, it points straight to neurasthenia. You're doing awesome. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T9#GNS314_U2_T9_h2)

question: Which bone forms the front boundary of the pelvic floor?

options.A: Coccyx
options.B: Pubic symphysis
options.C: Iliac crest
options.D: Ischial tuberosity

explanation: Great job! The pubic symphysis sits right at the front, marking the anterior boundary of the pelvis. You've got this! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T11#GNS121_U5_T11_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a consequence of poor specimen collection technique?

options.A: Prescription of incorrect antibiotics
options.B: Need for painful repeat sample collection
options.C: Immediate cure of the bacterial infection
options.D: Inaccurate laboratory test results

explanation: Bad collection leads to wrong results and wrong drugs, which makes the infection drag on—it definitely won't cure it! [learn more](GST114_U5_T1#GST114_U5_T1_h8)

question: What is the very first step in the MBO cycle within a healthcare organization?

options.A: Conducting the final end-of-year staff performance review
options.B: Purchasing new medical equipment for the wards
options.C: Executive leadership defining broad strategic goals
options.D: Punishing departments that failed previous targets

explanation: The MBO process starts at the top, giving a clear direction that individual departments can then break down. [learn more](GST321_U2_T5#GST321_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which of these actions is a big no-no for a nurse working in the public civil service?

options.A: Attending mandatory nursing professional update workshops
options.B: Requesting standard medical history data from a patient
options.C: Consulting senior colleagues regarding complex patient cases
options.D: Diverting public hospital drugs for personal commercial sale

explanation: Using government supplies or hospital drugs for your own personal business is a serious violation of civil service ethics. [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h4)

question: Why are the testes located outside the main body cavity in the scrotum?

options.A: To produce testosterone for secondary sex traits
options.B: To store mature sperm cells before ejaculation
options.C: To keep the testes cooler than core body temperature
options.D: To secrete fluid that forms the bulk of semen

explanation: You've got this! Sperm production works best at a slightly lower temperature than our normal body heat. That is why nature designed the scrotum to hang outside the body to keep the testes nice and cool. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T1#GNS311_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which nursing action is best for keeping track of a patient's ongoing nutrition?

options.A: Prescribing high-protein dietary supplements independently
options.B: Measuring indirect calorimetry on every single shift
options.C: Calculating precise basal metabolic rate without a formula
options.D: Recording daily weights and monitoring food intake

explanation: Never underestimate the basics! Daily weight checks and watching how much food actually gets eaten give nurses the best clues on nutritional health. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h7)

question: What is the main job of a mechanical ventilator in the ICU?

options.A: To replace the function of the human heart
options.B: To assist or take over the work of breathing
options.C: To increase blood pressure in shock patients
options.D: To cure underlying lung diseases permanently

explanation: Think of the ventilator as an extra pair of lungs! It helps or completely takes over breathing to keep oxygen flowing while the patient's body heals. You've got this! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T15#GNS212_U4_T15_h1)

question: Why is careful preparation a must before transferring an unstable disaster patient to another hospital?

options.A: It allows the nurse to take a long break during transport.
options.B: It ensures the receiving hospital never has to buy medical supplies.
options.C: Moving patients without stabilization and monitoring can lead to rapid clinical deterioration.
options.D: Transfer paperwork is the only legal requirement in disaster zones.

explanation: Correct! Bumping along in a vehicle can dislodge lines or worsen shock if the patient isn't properly stabilized and monitored before the journey begins. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T2#GNS315_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which clinical sign points more toward a clotting factor problem like haemophilia rather than a platelet issue?

options.A: Petechiae scattered across the lower legs
options.B: Frequent, mild nosebleeds that stop within minutes
options.C: Tiny red spots on the skin after minor pressure
options.D: Bleeding into large joints like the knees and elbows

explanation: Bleeding into big joints (called hemarthrosis) is a classic trademark of factor deficiencies like haemophilia. Petechiae and nosebleeds are usually more about platelet trouble. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T10#GNS311_U2_T10_h5)

question: Which body change happens as people grow older that tends to slow down drug clearance?

options.A: Faster production of stomach acid
options.B: Increased total body water volume
options.C: Enlarged total liver mass capacity
options.D: Decreased kidney filtration function

explanation: As we age, kidney function naturally slows down a bit. This means older adults take longer to clear medications from their system. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T10#GNS125_U5_T10_h2)

question: A clinic is in an area that floods every rainy season. What is the best structural safety step for them?

options.A: Issuing warning pamphlets to patients in the waiting room
options.B: Training nurses on how to swim in fast-moving water
options.C: Buying extra bandages and IV fluids for the pharmacy
options.D: Moving the emergency backup generators to an upper floor

explanation: Brilliant! Elevating power systems protects them from floodwaters so the clinic can keep running. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h3)

question: In nursing management, what do we mean by conflict "antecedents"?

options.A: The official disciplinary policies used after a fight occurs
options.B: The underlying conditions that create fertile ground for disputes
options.C: The emotional reactions patients have to hospital staff
options.D: The legal documents signed when a nurse is hired

explanation: Think of antecedents as the early sparks or background conditions that set the stage for a disagreement to happen later. Spotting them early helps you keep the ward peaceful! [learn more](GST321_U5_T2#GST321_U5_T2_h1)

question: What is a key part of a safe emergency obstetric referral from a community clinic?

options.A: Ensuring a trained health worker accompanies the patient
options.B: Sending the patient alone with a family member only
options.C: Withholding all intravenous fluids during transit
options.D: Waiting until daylight before arranging any travel

explanation: Brilliant! Having a trained provider ride along means vital signs are watched and complications like bleeding or seizures can be managed on the way. Teamwork saves lives! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h7)

question: Which health areas are most commonly supported by international donors and NGOs in Nigeria?

options.A: Specific disease programs like HIV/AIDS, malaria, and polio
options.B: Routine administrative salaries of state commissioners of health
options.C: Importation of luxury vehicles for hospital management boards
options.D: Construction of private mansions for retired medical directors

explanation: Correct! International partners love to channel their resources into major public health campaigns and infectious disease control. [learn more](GST322_U5_T4#GST322_U5_T4_h7)

question: What are the three classic actions that make NSAIDs a go-to drug class in clinical practice?

options.A: Muscle relaxation, sedation, and blood thinning
options.B: Blood pressure reduction, diuresis, and infection cure
options.C: Bronchodilation, mucus clearance, and cough suppression
options.D: Pain relief, fever reduction, and anti-inflammation

explanation: Remember the big three for NSAIDs: analgesics (pain), antipyretics (fever), and anti-inflammatories (swelling). You'll see these used everywhere on the ward! [learn more](GNS223_U5_T4#GNS223_U5_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary receptor targeted by Class II antiarrhythmic drugs?

options.A: Calcium binding sites
options.B: Potassium ion channels
options.C: Beta-adrenergic receptors
options.D: Sodium transport gates

explanation: Class II drugs are beta-blockers that attach to beta-adrenergic receptors to block the effects of adrenaline on the heart. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h4)

question: A student wants to study 'hospital stress'. Which option is a well-focused, realistic research topic?

options.A: Reviewing the history of global healthcare systems
options.B: Comparing the salaries of all hospital workers worldwide
options.C: Assessing night-shift burnout among intensive care unit nurses
options.D: Finding out why people get stressed in all buildings

explanation: Great research topics are narrow and specific! Focusing on a particular group (ICU nurses) and issue (night-shift burnout) makes your study much easier to manage. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T2#GNS224_U3_T2_h2)

question: What is the first step in conducting any cross-sectional study?

options.A: Defining the research question
options.B: Publishing the results in a journal
options.C: Analyzing the final statistics
options.D: Discharging the participating patients

explanation: Every great nursing project starts with a clear question. Once you know what you're asking, the path forward becomes much easier! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h4)

question: Why are daily full-body soap baths usually not recommended for frail elderly patients?

options.A: Elderly patients are completely immune to body odors
options.B: Water damages their internal organs through the skin pores
options.C: Their skin loses natural oils and becomes dry and irritated
options.D: Soap makes their bones become fragile and brittle

explanation: As skin ages, it makes fewer natural oils. Daily harsh soap and scrubbing can strip away what's left, leading to painful, dry, cracked skin. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h6)

question: What is the single best way to stop germs from spreading during patient care?

options.A: Avoiding all physical contact with patients
options.B: Performing proper hand hygiene
options.C: Wearing sterile gowns at all times
options.D: Using scented room sprays

explanation: Simple handwashing or using hand sanitiser is your superpower against infections. It washes away those sneaky microbes before they can jump to the next patient! [learn more](GNS124_U6_T3#GNS124_U6_T3_h3)

question: Which group of people is most vulnerable to problems with temperature regulation?

options.A: Young adults engaging in sports
options.B: Athletes with high muscle mass
options.C: Healthy adults working indoors
options.D: Elderly patients and infants

explanation: Spot on! Babies and older adults have a harder time adjusting to extreme temperatures, so we need to watch out for them. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T4#GNS211_U2_T4_h6)

question: Roughly what fraction of your total body water lives outside the cells (extracellular fluid)?

options.A: Three-quarters
options.B: One-half
options.C: Two-thirds
options.D: One-third

explanation: Spot on! About one-third of our body fluid flows outside the cells, while the other two-thirds stays safely inside. You've got this! [learn more](GNS121_U2_T10#GNS121_U2_T10_h1)

question: What is a major logistical problem caused by uncoordinated disaster donations?

options.A: Relief workers spend all their time cooking donated food
options.B: Local markets experience a permanent surplus of luxury vehicles
options.C: Hospitals run out of storage space for monetary funds
options.D: Unwanted goods block transport routes while essential items get stuck

explanation: Sending random unrequested supplies clogs up ports and roads, delaying the delivery of life-saving medical gear. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h6)

question: What is the bioavailability of a medication given directly through an intravenous (IV) line?

options.A: 10 percent
options.B: 100 percent
options.C: 50 percent
options.D: 0 percent

explanation: Because IV meds go straight into your veins, they bypass the gut and liver completely. That means 100% of the dose reaches your bloodstream instantly! [learn more](GNS125_U1_T4#GNS125_U1_T4_h7)

question: A nursing researcher wants to mark down the exact presence or absence of hand hygiene steps among ward staff during a shift. Which tool should they use?

options.A: Audio recording
options.B: Checklist
options.C: Unstructured narrative
options.D: Rating scale

explanation: Checklists are ideal for recording whether specific, distinct actions occurred or did not occur. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h3)

question: What happens inside lung cells when beta-2 receptors are stimulated?

options.A: An increase in intracellular cyclic AMP
options.B: The immediate destruction of lung tissue

question: Which brain structure acts as the main relay station for incoming sensory messages before they reach the cortex?

options.A: Hypothalamus
options.B: Cerebellum
options.C: Thalamus
options.D: Pons

explanation: Spot on! The thalamus is like a busy airport control tower, sorting and routing almost all incoming sensory signals to the correct spots in the brain. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T28#GNS211_U3_T28_h5)

question: Which characteristic is a core feature of a bureaucratic management structure?

options.A: Decisions based purely on personal friendships
options.B: Total freedom to ignore hospital policies
options.C: Constant shifting of job roles every single day
options.D: A strict hierarchy of authority

explanation: Bureaucracy relies heavily on a clear vertical chain of command and structured reporting lines. [learn more](GST321_U1_T3#GST321_U1_T3_h3)

question: Which of these is a clear example of artificial active immunity?

options.A: Getting a polio vaccine at the primary health clinic
options.B: Drinking colostrum from a mother immediately after birth
options.C: Catching chickenpox from a classmate at school
options.D: Receiving snake antivenom after a bite on the farm

explanation: Spot on! Vaccines introduce harmless germ parts (antigens) so your body actively builds its own defense. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T83#GNS214_U1_T83_h4)

question: What is the main focus of a system-based approach to medical errors?

options.A: Increasing the frequency of staff performance appraisals
options.B: Punishing the individual nurse who performed the task
options.C: Reducing the salary of workers involved in mistakes
options.D: Looking at flawed workflows and environmental factors

explanation: You nailed it! Instead of blaming one human being, a system approach looks at equipment, heavy workloads, and communication breakdowns. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h3)

question: Why might a patient show signs of a delayed transfusion reaction a few days after getting blood?

options.A: The patient forgot to take prescribed post-transfusion antibiotics
options.B: Low-level antibodies increased over time and attacked newly introduced cells
options.C: The blood bag was stored in a refrigerator that was too cold
options.D: The intravenous cannula was left in place for too many days

explanation: Sometimes antibodies are so low in number that lab tests miss them initially. Once exposed to the donor cells, those antibody levels rise and start a delayed attack. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T12#GNS311_U2_T12_h6)

question: When a woman is diagnosed with cervical cancer, which two cell types are most commonly involved?

options.A: Sarcoma and transitional cell carcinoma
options.B: Melanoma and small cell carcinoma
options.C: Squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma
options.D: Lymphoma and clear cell carcinoma

explanation: You've got this! Squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma make up the vast majority of cervical cancers. They develop from the two main types of cells found on the cervix. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h1)

question: A quiet elderly patient takes a normal sedative before a procedure and suddenly starts shouting. What is your best conclusion?

options.A: The medication dosage was clearly too low to be effective
options.B: The patient has developed an anaphylactic immune reaction
options.C: The patient is experiencing a rare idiosyncratic drug response
options.D: The patient is suffering from acute bacterial meningitis

explanation: Getting wild instead of sleepy from a sedative points right to a paradoxical idiosyncratic reaction. Spot on! [learn more](GNS125_U1_T7#GNS125_U1_T7_h4)

question: Why is a team approach involving different professions so important when helping trafficking survivors?

options.A: Doctors are legally barred from talking to police officers
options.B: No single profession has all the skills needed for complex recovery
options.C: Legal frameworks prevent nurses from providing basic medical care
options.D: Psychological counseling is the only treatment survivors require

explanation: Trafficked children have diverse medical, emotional, and legal needs that require different experts working together seamlessly. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T25#GNS225_U5_T25_h7)

question: What is a main objective of setting clinical standards in Quality Assurance?

options.A: Ensuring every nurse performs procedures the same safe way
options.B: Making sure doctors do all the documentation
options.C: Eliminating the need for patient handovers
options.D: Reducing the number of nursing shifts per week

explanation: Spot on! Clinical standards act like a reliable compass. They make sure that no matter who is on duty, every patient gets the same safe, top-notch care. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h2)

question: What does a pulse oximeter actually measure in the patient?

options.A: Exact blood pressure inside the artery
options.B: Total red blood cell count in the body
options.C: Oxygen saturation percentage in the blood
options.D: Carbon dioxide levels in the lungs

explanation: The device uses light absorption to estimate how much hemoglobin is carrying oxygen. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h2)

question: What minimum level of medication adherence is needed to keep HIV fully suppressed over the long term?

options.A: Around 50%
options.B: Exactly 20%
options.C: At least 95%
options.D: Only on weekends

explanation: You got it! HIV treatment requires consistency. Taking at least 95% of doses on schedule keeps the virus cornered and unable to fight back. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T4#GNS216_U6_T4_h8)

question: A nurse wants to chat with a patient across a state border using a regular social media app. What is the main risk here?

options.A: The phone battery will drain too quickly during the chat
options.B: Potential breach of privacy and possible licensing violations
options.C: The patient will refuse to take their prescribed medication
options.D: Social media apps always improve the accuracy of vital signs

explanation: Careful! Public social media apps aren't secure for health data, and practicing across regions without proper clearance can break professional rules. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h4)

question: A patient says her periods always arrive every 28 days, last 5 days, and have a moderate flow. What is your best initial nursing action?

options.A: Document this as a normal finding in her chart
options.B: Instruct her to start taking oral contraceptives
options.C: Order emergency hormone blood tests
options.D: Refer her immediately to a gynecological surgeon

explanation: A classic 28-day cycle with moderate flow is textbook normal! No interventions or emergency tests are needed—just a clean, accurate chart entry. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h7)

question: What happens if a bar chart's vertical scale doesn't start at zero?

options.A: The categories on the horizontal axis automatically disappear
options.B: The chart becomes a continuous line graph instead
options.C: Small differences between groups can look exaggerated and misleading
options.D: The total number of patients surveyed is cut in half

explanation: Starting a Y-axis above zero can play tricks on the eyes, making tiny gaps look like massive clinical differences. Always check that scale! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T7#GNS217_U4_T7_h2)

question: A patient comes in with a severe infection and a high fever. What should the nurse expect to happen to their metabolic rate?

options.A: Metabolic rate remains completely unchanged
options.B: Metabolic rate drops to zero
options.C: Metabolic rate increases significantly
options.D: Metabolic rate fluctuates only during sleep

explanation: Fever acts like stepping on the gas pedal for your cells! Chemical reactions speed up, which is why febrile patients burn through energy so fast. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h3)

question: Why is a low-residue (low-fiber, easy-to-digest) diet often given during a flare-up of inflammatory bowel disease?

options.A: To prevent the development of high blood pressure and fluid retention
options.B: To provide extra protein necessary for healing surgical incisions
options.C: To minimize mechanical irritation and reduce the workload on the inflamed bowel
options.D: To stimulate rapid weight loss and reduce overall body fat percentage

explanation: Think of it as giving the gut a gentle break. Low-residue foods leave very little waste behind, letting the sore, inflamed intestines rest and recover. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T008#GNS227_U7_T008_h5)

question: In community health financing, what does 'equity' mean?

options.A: Access to care depends on health needs rather than wealth
options.B: Hospitals receive equal funding regardless of patient volume
options.C: Every person pays the exact same amount of money
options.D: Wealthy individuals receive higher quality medical care

explanation: Think of equity as fairness! It ensures that financial barriers don't stop vulnerable people from getting the medical attention they require. [learn more](GST322_U4_T4#GST322_U4_T4_h2)

question: Which group has the most influence over traditional community practices concerning marriage?

options.A: Commercial banking executives
options.B: Traditional and religious leaders
options.C: International tourism boards
options.D: Foreign economic advisors

explanation: Traditional and religious leaders hold deep respect and authority in local communities, making their involvement key to changing harmful cultural practices. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T6#GNS225_U6_T6_h8)

question: You need to help move a heavy patient up in bed. Which of these follows safe ergonomic practices?

options.A: Holding the patient far away from the body to keep uniform clean
options.B: Bending sharply at the waist with straight knees to gain momentum
options.C: Twisting the torso quickly while lifting to reach the bedside table
options.D: Using a mechanical lift or asking a colleague for assistance

explanation: Never try to be a lone hero with heavy lifting! Always ask a colleague to team-lift or use mechanical aids to protect your lower back. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h5)

question: Which psychological condition is often seen in women and girls who have survived FGM?

options.A: Bipolar manic depression with hallucinations
options.B: Obsessive compulsive cleaning disorder
options.C: Post-traumatic stress disorder and anxiety
options.D: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder

explanation: Spot on! The painful and terrifying experience often leaves survivors with long-term emotional trauma, anxiety, and distress. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T1#GNS225_U6_T1_h5)

question: When do you need to use strict surgical asepsis instead of everyday medical asepsis?

options.A: Putting on clean gloves to empty a full bedpan
options.B: Inserting an indwelling urinary catheter into the bladder
options.C: Performing routine hand hygiene before feeding a patient
options.D: Wiping down a patient's bedside table with a disinfectant

explanation: Whenever you enter a sterile body tract like the bladder, you need absolute sterile technique to keep bacteria out. You've got this! [learn more](GST114_U2_T13#GST114_U2_T13_h1)

question: Why should you avoid giving rectal medications to a patient who has active rectal bleeding?

options.A: The patient will automatically develop an allergic reaction to the drug
options.B: The medication can worsen mucosal damage and might be washed away
options.C: The drug will bypass the liver entirely and cause immediate toxicity
options.D: The rectal sphincter will permanently lock shut and trap the medicine

explanation: Active bleeding or severe diarrhea stops the drug from being absorbed properly and can hurt the already irritated tissues. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a standard reason for routine lab testing in dairy production?

options.A: Checking for excessive bacterial load in raw milk supplies
options.B: Guaranteeing that the milk contains zero water molecules
options.C: Confirming the success of the pasteurization process
options.D: Verifying the overall sanitation of milking equipment

explanation: Spot on! Microbiological tests look for bacteria and check if pasteurization worked. Water content is measured separately using physics methods like cryoscopy, not germ tests! [learn more](GST114_U3_T4#GST114_U3_T4_h6)

question: When is it ethically okay for a nurse to open a patient's electronic health record?

options.A: Whenever the patient is a personal friend or family member
options.B: Only when actively involved in that patient's direct clinical care
options.C: During routine breaks to pass the time between shifts
options.D: At any time to satisfy personal curiosity about a diagnosis

explanation: Patient privacy is sacred! You should only look at records for patients you are directly caring for as part of your duties. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h5)

question: In an adult, around which part of the spine does the main spinal cord usually end?

options.A: Fifth thoracic vertebra
options.B: First lumbar vertebra
options.C: First sacral vertebra
options.D: Twelfth thoracic vertebra

explanation: Well done! The cord ends near L1, which is why doctors insert the needle lower down where it's safer. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T11#GNS222_U3_T11_h3)

question: Why is the sublingual route unsuitable for medications that require a large dose?

options.A: Large doses dissolve too quickly to be safe.
options.B: Large amounts will stain the teeth permanently.
options.C: Big pills cause the tongue to become paralyzed.
options.D: The physical space under the tongue is very small.

explanation: Only small, highly potent doses fit comfortably under the tongue for effective mucosal absorption. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h5)

question: In economics, what two things must a patient have for true 'demand' to exist?

options.A: Approval from a local health ministry
options.B: Immediate availability of a hospital bed
options.C: Financial ability and willingness to pay
options.D: A written referral from a senior physician

explanation: You've got it! Wanting care isn't enough in the market; you also need the means to pay for it. That's what economists call true demand. [learn more](GST322_U1_T2#GST322_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why must a community nurse look at social factors like poverty alongside clinical symptoms?

options.A: Clinical vital signs are completely useless without a university degree
options.B: Hospital management requires a list of every patient's religious beliefs
options.C: Social issues like poverty and poor housing often drive poor health outcomes
options.D: Social assessments replace the need to check blood pressure and pulse

explanation: A patient's living conditions tell half the story. If someone goes home to dirty water and no food, treating their illness at the clinic is only a temporary fix. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h4)

question: What is the main goal of maternal home healthcare visits in our communities?

options.A: To bridge the gap between hospital services and community living
options.B: To distribute free prescription drugs to every household
options.C: To replace the need for hospital delivery entirely
options.D: To enforce strict hospital rules inside family compounds

explanation: Home visits let you bring health education and monitoring right to the doorstep of mothers who find it hard to visit the clinic regularly. You're making healthcare accessible where they live! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h1)

question: Why is psychological safety important for nursing staff?

options.A: It prevents patients from ever experiencing any clinical complications
options.B: It guarantees that nurses will receive a salary increase every year
options.C: It allows nurses to report near misses and errors without fear of unfair punishment
options.D: It eliminates the need for doctors to supervise nursing procedures

explanation: When nurses feel safe from unfair punishment, they freely report near misses. This helps the whole team spot hazards and keep patients safe. [learn more](GST319_U6_T3#GST319_U6_T3_h3)

question: A patient's IVP report notes a 'filling defect' in the right ureter. What condition is the radiologist most likely describing?

options.A: An abnormal mass or kidney stone taking up space
options.B: An area where the contrast dye failed to reach at all
options.C: A normal pocket of air trapped inside the bladder
options.D: A normal variation in the size of the right kidney

explanation: A filling defect is an area where something like a stone or tumor displaces the contrast dye, creating a dark spot on the x-ray film. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h8)

question: Which part of the glucometer setup has the chemical reagents that react with blood?

options.A: The digital display
options.B: The test strip
options.C: The lancet needle
options.D: The battery compartment

explanation: The test strip does the heavy lifting! It contains special enzymes that react with the glucose in the blood sample. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h2)

question: Why do nurses auscultate (listen) before palpating (feeling) the abdomen?

options.A: To make the patient feel warmer
options.B: Because palpation takes too long to finish
options.C: To prevent the stethoscope from getting dirty
options.D: To avoid altering natural bowel sounds

explanation: If you press or rub the belly first (palpation), you wake up the intestines and create fake bowel sounds. Always listen first so you hear what's naturally going on! [learn more](GNS124_U6_T3#GNS124_U6_T3_h4)

question: When taking a sexual history from a patient, what is the best interviewing style to use?

options.A: Asking rapid closed-ended questions to get through the interview quickly
options.B: Expressing personal moral disapproval to encourage future safe behaviour
options.C: Avoiding questions about anal or oral practices to prevent client embarrassment
options.D: Using a neutral, non-judgmental tone and asking open-ended questions

explanation: As nurses, we keep our personal biases out of the room. A warm, open approach makes the patient trust you enough to tell the whole truth. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T3#GNS216_U5_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of the community health planning cycle?

options.A: To replace traditional healers with orthodox medical practitioners
options.B: To punish communities that fail to follow sanitation guidelines
options.C: To systematically address population health problems using available resources
options.D: To increase the patient admission rates in tertiary hospitals

explanation: The planning cycle provides a structured framework for public health nurses to tackle community-wide health issues efficiently. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h1)

question: What is the standard rule for turning a bed-bound patient to help prevent pressure sores?

options.A: Every two hours
options.B: Every six hours
options.C: Once per shift
options.D: Only when they complain of pain

explanation: Turning a patient at least every two hours takes the weight off vulnerable spots, giving blood flow a chance to rush back in and save the skin. Simple and life-saving! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h6)

question: Why is it best to use short, simple sentences when talking to a patient in a full-blown panic attack?

options.A: Short sentences prevent the nurse from becoming overly anxious as well.
options.B: Patients with panic disorders have difficulty hearing long words.
options.C: Simple sentences make the patient fall asleep immediately.
options.D: Patients in panic have impaired cognitive processing and cannot handle complex information.

explanation: When panic takes over, the brain is flooded with fear and cannot process long explanations. Keep your words brief, clear, and easy to digest. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T10#GNS123_U3_T10_h7)

question: What is the age range for adolescents according to the World Health Organization?

options.A: 5 to 12 years old
options.B: 18 to 25 years old
options.C: 10 to 19 years old
options.D: 13 to 30 years old

explanation: The World Health Organization specifically defines the adolescent bracket as spanning from age 10 through 19. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T1#GNS312_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why is knowing about negative feedback helpful in nursing care?

options.A: It proves hormones only work through nerves.
options.B: It explains why a struggling gland often causes the brain to pump out more stimulating hormones.
options.C: It means nurses never have to check lab results.
options.D: It keeps blood sugar high during exercise.

explanation: Brilliant! Because of negative feedback, if a target gland fails, the brain tries harder by sending out more stimulating hormones to compensate. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T1#GNS211_U1_T1_h7)

question: What actually defines an ethical dilemma in nursing?

options.A: A situation where two or more moral principles conflict with each other
options.B: A disagreement between a nurse and a doctor over medication dosage
options.C: A patient refusing to pay their nursing agency bills
options.D: A broken piece of medical equipment inside the patient's home

explanation: Spot on! It's a tough spot where every choice seems to break a moral rule, and there is no easy right or wrong answer. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T10#GNS324_U1_T10_h8)

question: What is a common result of supportive and transformational leadership on a hospital ward?

options.A: More communication breakdowns among health workers
options.B: Higher rates of preventable patient falls
options.C: Increased staff turnover and frequent nurse burnout
options.D: Lower medication errors and higher staff satisfaction

explanation: Supportive leadership builds a safe reporting culture and teamwork, which reduces errors and keeps nurses happy. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h7)

question: What is the main goal of routine health check-ups in the workplace?

options.A: To determine the exact monthly salary of each employee
options.B: To help the company fire workers who take sick leave
options.C: To diagnose unrelated personal illnesses like childhood malaria
options.D: To detect early signs of work-related illness before permanent damage occurs

explanation: Early detection is key in nursing! Routine checks catch small health issues early on, stopping them from turning into major, long-term illnesses. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h5)

question: What is the most serious and dangerous complication that can happen after a gastrointestinal dilation?

options.A: Mild throat irritation
options.B: Temporary hiccups
options.C: Visceral perforation
options.D: Dry mouth sensation

explanation: Perforation means a tear or hole gets poked through the wall of the esophagus or bowel. It's a medical emergency that happens if the tissue tears during stretching. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T19#GNS212_U1_T19_h6)

question: Why do some experienced healthcare staff initially resist shifting from paper charts to electronic health records?

options.A: They are legally forbidden by hospital policy from touching computer keyboards
options.B: They believe digital records make patient care completely invisible to doctors
options.C: They are comfortable with traditional paper habits and fear learning complex new software
options.D: They prefer spending extra hours manually searching through heavy filing cabinets

explanation: Change management is difficult because staff accustomed to paper workflows often feel intimidated or inconvenienced by new technology. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which situation can instantly plunge a family into a deep emotional crisis?

options.A: Attending a community health talk
options.B: Going for a routine yearly check-up at the clinic
options.C: Learning how to take home medications properly
options.D: A main breadwinner getting hit with a serious, long-term illness

explanation: When unexpected illness strikes the person providing for the home, it shatters family stability and money security all at once. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h6)

question: A research group finds a questionnaire that was super reliable in the US ten years ago. Why must they test its reliability again for a new local study?

options.A: Hospital ethics committees require a new test to pay the researchers
options.B: Published research papers automatically expire after five years
options.C: Cultural differences and demographics can change how the tool performs
options.D: Statistical formulas change every decade to match new computer systems

explanation: Reliability isn't a permanent stamp of approval. A tool that works great in one culture or setting might need re-testing to prove it fits a different local population. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T27#GNS224_U1_T27_h7)

question: What is the best nursing action when family members are scared of casual contact with an HIV-positive relative?

options.A: Prescribe prophylactic antibiotics for everyone living in the house
options.B: Report the family to social welfare for discriminatory behavior
options.C: Provide clear education on how the virus is actually transmitted
options.D: Advise the patient to move out to protect the relatives

explanation: Spot on! Clearing up myths with gentle facts helps chase away fear and stops unnecessary separation at home. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T6#GNS216_U6_T6_h4)

question: What is the main public health approach used to control schistosomiasis in heavily affected communities?

options.A: Widespread daily chlorine spraying of all farmlands
options.B: Mandatory quarantine of all infected families
options.C: Mass drug administration of praziquantel
options.D: Surgical removal of adult worms from patients

explanation: Instead of waiting for individuals to fall sick, health teams treat whole communities—especially school children—all at once to knock down the disease burden. Brilliant public health strategy! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h8)

question: Which deficiency disease is caused by a serious lack of Vitamin C?

options.A: Beriberi
options.B: Rickets
options.C: Scurvy
options.D: Pellagra

explanation: You got it! Without enough Vitamin C, your body can't make collagen properly, leading to scurvy (bleeding gums and slow-healing wounds). [learn more](GNS227_U1_T008#GNS227_U1_T008_h7)

question: What is the primary focus of qualitative research methods?

options.A: Calculating patient weights on a digital scale
options.B: Exploring human experiences and meanings in depth
options.C: Measuring precise chemical levels in the blood
options.D: Counting the exact number of pills in a bottle

explanation: That's right! Qualitative research helps us understand people's feelings, stories, and subjective experiences. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T20#GNS224_U1_T20_h4)

question: What is the main goal of giving Oral Rehydration Therapy (ORT)?

options.A: To stop the bowels from moving immediately
options.B: To replace lost fluids and electrolytes using the gut
options.C: To kill the bacteria causing the stomach infection
options.D: To provide full daily nutritional calories

explanation: Spot on! ORT uses the body's natural drinking process to safely put back all the water and essential mineral salts that were washed away. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h2)

question: What complication can develop in a patient who suffers from severe, unmanaged fear throughout a long hospital stay?

options.A: Complete immunity to all future bacterial infections
options.B: Post-traumatic stress symptoms related to the medical experience
options.C: Instant recovery from chronic respiratory illnesses
options.D: Permanent loss of the sense of taste and smell

explanation: Well done! Extreme, unmanaged distress during medical care can unfortunately leave long-lasting psychological scars. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T11#GNS123_U3_T11_h7)

question: Which of these nursing examples uses a quantitative design?

options.A: Recording a journal of daily emotional struggles during grief counseling
options.B: Observing nurse-patient interactions during a busy ward handover
options.C: Measuring hourly blood sugar levels after giving a new insulin dose
options.D: Interviewing elderly patients about their childhood memories of illness

explanation: Tracking blood sugar gives you clear numbers that you can run statistics on—that is the classic sign of quantitative research. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T6#GNS224_U1_T6_h2)

question: What do we call the unwritten rules and expected behaviors in a community?

options.A: Boundaries
options.B: Statutes
options.C: Norms
options.D: Values

explanation: Norms are simply the everyday social habits and acceptable behaviors shared by a cultural group. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T3#GNS225_U1_T3_h4)

question: A community health nurse is planning care in a village near a fast-flowing river. Which action best supports primary prevention?

options.A: Isolating infected patients in hospital wards for six months
options.B: Administering daily eye drops to every school-aged child
options.C: Educating residents on wearing protective clothing and using ivermectin
options.D: Surgically removing all subcutaneous nodules from every villager

explanation: Teaching folks how to avoid blackfly bites and combining that with community ivermectin distribution is the gold standard in public health nursing. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T7#GNS214_U1_T7_h6)

question: A wheelchair user visits the clinic complaining of unusual fatigue and constant thirst. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Investigate for potential systemic issues like diabetes
options.B: Refer the patient immediately to an orthotic specialist
options.C: Advise the patient to rest more and avoid further medical testing
options.D: Document that fatigue is a normal side effect of using a wheelchair

explanation: Never brush off new symptoms! Fatigue and thirst could mean something like diabetes, so they always deserve a proper check-up. You're thinking like a real nurse! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T15#GNS225_U5_T15_h2)

question: What is '360-degree feedback' in a nursing performance review?

options.A: Asking the head of nursing to observe a nurse from all angles
options.B: Rotating a nurse through every department in the hospital for a day
options.C: Gathering performance input from peers, patients, and other team members
options.D: Measuring how many degrees a nurse can bend during physical therapy

explanation: Think of it as getting the full picture! Instead of just your boss judging you, feedback comes from colleagues, patients, and doctors who work closely with you. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h3)

question: Which IV fluid is the ONLY one safe to use alongside blood products?

options.A: Ringer's Lactate Solution
options.B: 0.9% Normal Saline
options.C: 5% Dextrose in Water
options.D: Half-Normal Saline

explanation: Normal saline is isotonic and friendly to red blood cells, preventing them from bursting or clumping like other fluids might. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T18#GNS122_U1_T18_h4)

question: Why does very little blood flow through the fetal lungs before birth?

options.A: The liver absorbs all the blood first
options.B: The heart pumps too weakly to reach the chest
options.C: The lungs are filled with fluid and do not exchange gas

options.A: Caregivers often notice daily challenges that clinical tests miss
options.B: Family members are legally required to sign all charts
options.C: Relatives can perform physical therapy instead of professionals
options.D: It reduces the total cost of purchasing hospital equipment

explanation: Great job! Families live closely with the patient, so they give us real-life insights that a quick check in the clinic might completely miss. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why is 'milieu therapy' considered such an important part of psychiatric nursing?

options.A: It turns the entire ward environment into a safe, healing space
options.B: It guarantees that patients will never experience distress
options.C: It replaces the need for doctors to prescribe medications
options.D: It focuses exclusively on heavy physical fitness routines

explanation: Milieu therapy uses your surroundings! By keeping the ward structured, safe, and supportive, staff and patient interactions combine to encourage healing and positive social habits. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T1#GNS314_U1_T1_h7)

question: Why are individuals with pre-existing mental health conditions especially vulnerable during disasters?

options.A: They are completely immune to physical injuries
options.B: Disasters automatically cure their psychiatric symptoms
options.C: Their usual support systems and medication routines are often disrupted
options.D: Emergency workers always prioritize them over everyone else

explanation: When clinics close, pharmacies run out of stock, and daily structures collapse, stable mental health conditions can quickly deteriorate. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h4)

question: Where is the normal point of maximal impulse (PMI) located on a healthy adult chest?

options.A: Second intercostal space at the left sternal border
options.B: Third intercostal space at the right sternal border
options.C: Seventh intercostal space at the anterior axillary line
options.D: Fifth intercostal space at the left midclavicular line

explanation: You'll usually find the normal PMI right at the fifth intercostal space along the left midclavicular line. Excellent clinical landmark! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h7)

question: A student proposes to study 'every health issue affecting every patient in the country.' What is the main problem with this topic?

options.A: The methodology uses too many statistical tests
options.B: It focuses too much on ethical patient consent
options.C: It relies entirely on recent nursing journals
options.D: The scope is far too broad to be manageable

explanation: A good proposal needs a narrow, focused topic so you can actually finish it successfully without getting overwhelmed! [learn more](GNS224_U3_T1#GNS224_U3_T1_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of doing a colonoscopy?

options.A: Viewing the entire colon lining and removing polyps
options.B: Flushing out impacted stool from the small intestine
options.C: Measuring the exact pressure inside the stomach
options.D: Checking liver enzymes through a small tissue sample

explanation: Well done! A colonoscopy allows the doctor to use a tiny camera scope to look directly at the large bowel lining, take tissue samples, or safely remove growths. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h2)

question: What is considered the single most effective way to stop the spread of infections in a hospital?

options.A: Wearing heavy utility gloves all day
options.B: Frequent and proper hand hygiene
options.C: Administering prophylactic antibiotics
options.D: Changing bed linens every morning

explanation: Never underestimate the power of clean hands! Good hand hygiene washes away transient germs before they can travel from patient to patient. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T4#GNS122_U4_T4_h5)

question: After a flood, a local youth group sets up a shared cooking space and organizes games for displaced children. Which MHPSS tier does this fit?

options.A: Tier 3
options.B: Tier 2
options.C: Tier 4
options.D: Tier 1

explanation: Great job! Activities that bring people together, rebuild routines, and foster community support belong right in Tier 2. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T5#GNS314_U6_T5_h3)

question: If a factory worker is exposed to loud industrial noise for years, which part of the cochlea usually shows damage first?

options.A: The base near the oval window, which processes high frequencies
options.B: The round window membrane protecting the lower cochlear chamber
options.C: The scala media endolymph ducts located in the middle turn
options.D: The apex near the helicotrema, which processes low frequencies

explanation: The base of the cochlea receives high-frequency sounds first as they enter, making it the most vulnerable spot for noise-induced hearing loss. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T7#GNS211_U4_T7_h5)

question: You are giving bed bath care to an unconscious patient with a head injury. Which nursing action is most important?

options.A: Massaging the back vigorously to improve general circulation
options.B: Washing the face with cold water to stimulate consciousness
options.C: Removing the cervical collar to wash the neck thoroughly
options.D: Preventing sudden neck twisting and keeping the head aligned

explanation: Well done! Keeping the head and neck straight and neutral stops the neck veins from getting squeezed, which prevents sudden, dangerous spikes in brain pressure. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T13#GNS222_U3_T13_h6)

question: Why must a research project always be done in a systematic, step-by-step way?

options.A: To prevent the researcher from talking to patients
options.B: To make the final written report look very long
options.C: To ensure steps happen in a logical, orderly sequence
options.D: To make data analysis completely unnecessary

explanation: Exactly! Being systematic keeps everything organized and orderly so that anyone reading your study can follow what you did. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T1#GNS217_U2_T1_h2)
